root_cause.text: The `name_size` function in `tpm2-sessions.c` indexed a static array using the TPM algorithm ID without bounds checking, allowing out-of-range access when an unrecognized algorithm is supplied, potentially causing memory corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The original code used `static u8 size_map[] = { [TPM_ALG_SHA1] = ..., ... };` and then `return size_map[alg] + 2;` without validating `alg`. The CVE description states: "'name_size' does not have any range checks, and it just directly indexes with TPM_ALG_ID, which could lead into memory corruption at worst." The patch replaces this with a switch statement that returns `-EINVAL` for default/unrecognized values and makes all callers handle errors.

candidates.rationale: Directly indexes the static array size_map using alg without bounds checking, causing out-of-bounds access when alg is not a recognized TPM algorithm.
Extracts the algorithm ID from the name buffer without validation; this value is used as an index into size_map, enabling out-of-bounds access.
Calls name_size with a name that may come from an untrusted source (TPM response or user), leading to out-of-bounds memory access if the name's algorithm ID is invalid.
Uses name_size on data read from a TPM response buffer; an invalid algorithm ID in the name will cause out-of-bounds read within name_size.
Calls name_size on a name previously stored from a TPM operation; if the TPM provided an invalid algorithm ID, this triggers out-of-bounds access.
Declaration of the static array that is indexed without bounds checking; the array's size is determined by the initializers, but no guard exists for indices beyond those.

Author: James Bottomley <James.Bottomley@HansenPartnership.com>

    tpm: Add HMAC session name/handle append
    
    Add tpm2_append_name() for appending to the handle area of the TPM
    command.  When TPM_BUS_SECURITY is enabled and HMAC sessions are in
    use this adds the standard u32 handle to the buffer but additionally
    records the name of the object which must be used as part of the HMAC

bic_trace_step.reason: The `name_size` function introduced in this commit uses a static array `size_map` indexed by the algorithm ID from the name, without bounds checking. If an unrecognized algorithm ID is supplied (e.g., a value not equal to TPM_ALG_SHA1, SHA256, SHA384, or SHA512), it will index out of bounds of the array, causing memory corruption. The function does not include any check to verify that the algorithm ID is within the valid range before accessing the array. This is the vulnerable construct described in the root cause, and no fix is present in this commit.
